bibl.title: Reactivation of hippocampal ensemble memories during sleep

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the activity correlations between pairs of hippocampal CA1 cells, measured across sleep before behaviour, behaviour, and sleep after it
span.quote: Spike-train cross-correlations were computed for all pairs of principal cells during the pre-behavioral sleep (PRE) , running (RUN), and post-behavioral sleep (POST) periods.

span.label: whether the interactions among hippocampal cells change in a way SPECIFIC to the experience just had, rather than changing in general
span.quote: there has been no demonstration of changes in functional interaction among hippocampal cells specific to the representation of a given experience (3).

span.label: the first demonstration that cells coactive during behaviour become more correlated in the sleep that follows, while cells that were active and NOT coactive do not
span.quote: Cells that were coactive during behavior showed a significant increase in correlation from their PRE level compared to pairs in which both cells displayed spatial firing but not in the same region of space (11).

span.label: existence
span.quote: Cells that were coactive during behavior showed a significant increase in correlation from their PRE level compared to pairs in which both cells displayed spatial firing but not in the same region of space (11).

span.label: hippocampal ensemble reactivation during sleep
span.quote: On the hypothesis that hippocampal activity during sleep reflects the reactivation of population events representing the experiences of the prior waking behavior, cell pairs that were coactive during the RUN phase (because of their place field overlap) were examined during the POST phase and compared with cell pairs that were active but not coactive during behavior (non-overlapping place fields) (Figs. 2 and 3).

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: With the use of multielectrcde recording techniques (4), the activity of 50 to 100 single cells in area CAI of the hippocampus was monitored simultaneously during sleep periods before and after brief behavioral episodes (Fig. 1).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Waking experience drives associative synaptic modification, which leaves cells that were coactive during behaviour more likely to be reactivated together in subsequent slow-wave sleep
span.quote: This effect, which declined gradually during each post-behaviorsleep session, may resultfrom synaptic modificationduringwaking experience.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Event memory is first stored by rapid synaptic modification in the hippocampus, and is then replayed during slow-wave sleep (when further hippocampal modification is suppressed) so that the information is gradually transferred to neocortex
span.quote: During subsequent slow-wave sleep, synaptic moditication within the hippocampus itself is suppressed (16) and the neuronal states encoded within the hippocampus are "played back" as part of a consolidation process by which hippocampal information is gradually transferred to, the neocortex (6, 17).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Initial storage of the event occurs through rapid synaptic modification primarily within the hippocampus itself
span.quote: According to the proposed hypothesis, initial storage of event memory occurs through rapid synaptic modification, primarily within the hippocampus.

span.label: an autoassociative network in which RECURRENT EXCITATION reproduces a stored activity pattern from very little input - so background noise alone can push the network into a stored state, seen as a population burst
span.quote: consistent with previous theoretical models of autoassociative memory (6), in which recurrent excitation is used to reproduce a previously stored activity pattern, even when the input contains very little of the relevant information.

span.label: random background noise occasionally lands the network in a correlated state, and the resulting population bursts ARE the ripples - the paper's account of why the effect appears in discrete events rather than continuously
span.quote: In such networks, even random background noise can occasionally lead to the emergence of correlated states, manifested as population bursts (ripples), reflecting stored patterns.

span.label: storage is fast synaptic modification in the hippocampus during waking; sleep is the playback, and the transfer target is neocortex
span.quote: According to the proposed hypothesis, initial storage of event memory occurs through rapid synaptic modification, primarily within the hippocampus.

span.label: The increased correlation implies associative synaptic change somewhere in the system, but not necessarily inside the hippocampus.
span.quote: The inaeased melation is consistent with an underlying associative synaptic modification at some stage in the system, although not necessarily in the hippocampus.

span.label: Neocortical or subcortical changes are an alternative source of the increased correlations.
span.quote: Changes in neocortical or subcortical pathways might underlie the increased correlations.

span.label: THE PAPER REFUSES TO LOCATE ITS OWN MECHANISM. The increased correlation is called consistent with associative synaptic modification `at some stage in the system, ALTHOUGH NOT NECESSARILY IN THE HIPPOCAMPUS` - the structure it recorded from
span.quote: is consistent with an underlying associative synaptic modification at some stage in the system, although not necessarily in the hippocampus.

span.label: a PAIR-WISE correlation cannot show that the activity is organised into a coherent representation; the paper says the prior single-cell result was suggestive and could not settle it, which is the same limit its own measure has
span.quote: there has been no demonstration of changes in functional interaction among hippocampal cells specific to the representation of a given experience (3).

span.label: the population encoding any one event is expected to be small, so the whole design depends on recording enough cells for the pair count to grow as the square
span.quote: However, because the expected number of cells involved in encoding any particular event is small (4, 6)

span.label: cell pairs that were ACTIVE during running but NOT COACTIVE - non-overlapping place fields - are measured through the same PRE and POST sleep sessions as the coactive pairs
span.note: eliminates: any explanation that would raise correlations across the board: arousal, electrode drift, general post-behaviour excitability, or a recording artefact of the sleep session itself · outcome: held
span.quote: cell pairs that were coactive during the RUN phase (because of their place field overlap) were examined during the POST phase and compared with cell pairs that were active but not coactive during behavior (non-overlapping place fields) (Figs. 2 and 3).

span.label: the RUN phase is checked first for the effect the sorting assumes - that overlapping place fields do produce correlated firing and non-overlapping ones do not
span.note: eliminates: a sort that does not separate what it claims to, which would make the POST comparison meaningless in either direction · outcome: held
span.quote: During the RUN phase, as expected, cells with overlapping place fields exhibited highly positively correlated activity, whereas cell pairs with nonoverlapping fields did not exhibit such activity (Fig. 3).

span.label: the correlation is computed separately DURING ripples and in the intervals between them
span.note: eliminates: an effect spread evenly through sleep, which would not support the proposed burst-based transfer mechanism · outcome: absent-not-in-staged-text
span.quote: To investigate this hypothesis, correlation effects were examined both during ripples and during the intervals between them.

span.label: whether the correlation increase can be localised to the hippocampus at all
span.note: eliminates: nothing - the paper states the modification may be at some other stage in the system · outcome: absent-declared-unreported
span.quote: is consistent with an underlying associative synaptic modification at some stage in the system, although not necessarily in the hippocampus.

span.label: place fields
span.quote: During the RUN phase, as expected, cells with overlapping place fields exhibited highly positively correlated activity, whereas cell pairs with nonoverlapping fields did not exhibit such activity (Fig. 3).

span.label: cross-correlations
span.quote: Spike-train cross-correlations were computed for all pairs of principal cells during the pre-behavioral sleep (PRE) , running (RUN), and post-behavioral sleep (POST) periods.

span.label: ripples
span.quote: During slow-wave sleep, cells discharge in intermittent, synchronized bursts (ripples) (9), associated with electroencephalogram (EEG) sharp-wave (SPW) activity.

span.label: autoassociative memory
span.quote: consistent with previous theoretical models of autoassociative memory (6), in which recurrent excitation is used to reproduce a previously stored activity pattern, even when the input contains very little of the relevant information.

span.label: synaptic modification
span.quote: is consistent with an underlying associative synaptic modification at some stage in the system, although not necessarily in the hippocampus.

span.label: reactivation - AS MEASURED HERE: an increase in the short-latency cross-correlation of a cell PAIR from PRE to POST sleep. Not a replayed sequence, not a retrieved memory, not a hippocampal event specifically - the instrument sees a pair statistic and the title names a memory. The paper marks that gap twice rather than closing it
span.quote: is consistent with an underlying associative synaptic modification at some stage in the system, although not necessarily in the hippocampus.

span.label: memory, AS THE PAPER USES IT HERE: `the structure of distributed representations of the visited locations`, retained across sleep. The definition is spatial and population-level, and it is what the overlap-sorted pairs operationalise
span.quote: foregoing observations demonstrate that, during sleep, the activity of hippocampal cells engaged in place-specific activity during prior waking (5) retains the structure of distributed representations of the visited locations (Fig. 4).

span.label: ripple - a synchronised intermittent burst during slow-wave sleep, identified with the EEG sharp wave. Used here as the WINDOW in which the correlation effect is concentrated, and as the network signature of a stored pattern being re-entered
span.quote: During slow-wave sleep, cells discharge in intermittent, synchronized bursts (ripples) (9), associated with electroencephalogram (EEG) sharp-wave (SPW) activity.

span.label: the ripple/inter-ripple split - the paper's own test of where in sleep the effect lives. The design is stated plainly; its RESULT is the one sentence in this record that OCR damage puts out of reach, and the control below says so rather than borrowing a verdict from its neighbour
span.quote: To investigate this hypothesis, correlation effects were examined both during ripples and during the intervals between them.

span.label: claim_type: existence
span.note: a second reading reaching the same value. Recorded: existence — a second reading reaching the same value from a different sentence. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: there has been no demonstration of changes in functional interaction among hippocampal cells specific to the representation of a given experience (3).

span.label: method: simultaneous recording of 50 to 100 CA1 cells, short-latency spike-train cross-correlation computed per pair over each of three phases, pairs sorted by how much their place fields overlap
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: electrophysiology — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: Spike-train cross-correlations were computed for all pairs of principal cells during the pre-behavioral sleep (PRE) , running (RUN), and post-behavioral sleep (POST) periods.

span.label: phenomenon: experience-specific reactivation - coactivity acquired during waking behaviour re-expressed in hippocampal circuits during subsequent slow-wave sleep
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: hippocampal ensemble reactivation during sleep — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: foregoing observations demonstrate that, during sleep, the activity of hippocampal cells engaged in place-specific activity during prior waking (5) retains the structure of distributed representations of the visited locations (Fig. 4).

span.label: builds-on → previous theoretical models of autoassociative memory (ref. 6)
span.quote: This difTerence is consistent with previous theoretical models of autoassociative memory (6), in which recurrent excitation is used to reproduce a previously stored activity pattern, even when the input contains very little of the relevant information.

span.label: extends → the large-ensemble recording method itself, used here because the number of observable pair-wise interactions grows as the square of the cells recorded - the argument that makes an experience-specific effect measurable at all
span.quote: we have studied the activity correlations among large sets of simultaneously recorded cells (4), because the number of possible interactions that can be observed increases as the square of the sample size.

span.label: critiques → the indirect synaptic-efficacy evidence for hippocampal learning, on the ground that no change had been shown that was SPECIFIC to a given experience
span.quote: there has been no demonstration of changes in functional interaction among hippocampal cells specific to the representation of a given experience (3).

span.label: supports → autoassociative network models in which recurrent excitation reconstructs a stored pattern from little input
span.quote: consistent with previous theoretical models of autoassociative memory (6), in which recurrent excitation is used to reproduce a previously stored activity pattern, even when the input contains very little of the relevant information.

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: Cells that were correlated (OVR, solid bars) during the RUN phase exhibited a significant (analysis of variance, P < 0.05) increase in correlation during the post-run (POST) sleep relative to pre-run (PRE) sleep (*) or to cells that were non-overlapped (NON, hollow bars), and hence uncorrelated during running (plus signs).

span.label: cross-correlation
span.quote: Spike-train cross-correlations were computed for all pairs of principal cells during the pre-behavioral sleep (PRE) , running (RUN), and post-behavioral sleep (POST) periods.

span.label: mean

span.label: cross-correlations
span.quote: Spike-train cross-correlations were computed for all pairs of principal cells during the pre-behavioral sleep (PRE) , running (RUN), and post-behavioral sleep (POST) periods.

span.label: correlation
span.quote: Cells that were coactive during behavior showed a significant increase in correlation from their PRE level compared to pairs in which both cells displayed spatial firing but not in the same region of space (11).

span.label: Hippocampal CA1 cells that fired together during a spatial behavioural task showed increased tendency to fire together in the sleep that followed, relative to the sleep that preceded the task.
span.quote: Cells that fired together when the animal occupied particular locations in the environment exhibitedan increasedtendencyto fire together duringsubsequent sleep, in comparison to sleep episodes precedingthe behavioraltasks.

span.label: The increase was specific to coactive pairs: cells silent during behaviour, and active cells whose place fields did not overlap, showed no such increase.
span.quote: Cells that were inactive during behavior, or that were active but had non-overlappingspatial firing, did not show this increase.

span.label: Coactive (overlapping place field) pairs rose significantly above their pre-behaviour correlation level, whereas pairs of spatially firing cells with non-overlapping fields did not.
span.quote: Cells that were coactive during behavior showed a significant increase in correlation from their PRE level compared to pairs in which both cells displayed spatial firing but not in the same region of space (11).

span.label: The reactivation effect decayed across the post-behaviour sleep session with a time constant of about 12 minutes.
span.quote: This selective reactivation of correlated states declined during the POST phase with a time constant of approximately 12 min (1 2).

span.label: The sleep correlations were concentrated in the synchronized population bursts (ripples) rather than in the intervals between them.
span.quote: Correlations were signiiicantly larger during ripples than in the intervening intervals (14).

span.label: During running, cells with overlapping place fields were strongly positively correlated while non-overlapping pairs were not, confirming the grouping used for the sleep comparison.
span.quote: During the RUN phase, as expected, cells with overlapping place fields exhibited highly positively correlated activity, whereas cell pairs with nonoverlapping fields did not exhibit such activity (Fig. 3).

span.label: cells coactive during behaviour show a SIGNIFICANT INCREASE in correlation from PRE to POST sleep, and pairs that fired spatially but not in the same region do not - the effect is specific to shared experience, not to having been active
